record.original_question: Let C(m,n,N) denote the number of m x n Golomb rectangles containing N dots, where a Golomb rectangle is a rectangular dot pattern whose autocorrelation takes exactly the three values {N, 1, 0}. Determine C(m,n,N). In particular, for fixed m and n find the largest N with C(m,n,N) > 0, and for fixed N find the smallest m and n with C(m,n,N) > 0.

evidence.quote: Definition 12. A Golomb rectangle [83] is a rectangular array of N > 2 dots and blanks such that its auto-correlation range consists of exactly three values: {N, 1, 0}.

Problem 23. Let C(m, n, N) stand for the number of m × n Golomb rectangles containing N dots. Calculate C(m, n, N), and, in particular, for given m and n, find the maximal N for which C(m, n, N) > 0. Conversely, for a given N, find the smallest values of m and n for which C(m, n, N) > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A two-dimensional binary pattern is an m×n array A = (a_{i,j}) with entries in {0,1}, where the 1's are called "dots" and the 0's are called "blanks". The (discrete) autocorrelation of A is the function defined, for integer shifts (s,t) with |s|<m and |t|<n, by

  R(s,t) = Σ_{i,j} a_{i,j} · a_{i+s,j+t},

where a_{k,l} = 0 whenever (k,l) lies outside the m×n grid. Let N be the number of dots in A (so R(0,0)=N). Call A an m×n Golomb rectangle (with N dots) if N > 2 and the set of values { R(s,t) : (s,t) ranges over all admissible shifts } equals exactly {N, 1, 0}; equivalently, every nonzero shift of A overlaps the original pattern in either exactly one dot or no dots.

Let C(m,n,N) denote the number of m×n Golomb rectangles containing exactly N dots (counted as labeled subsets of the m×n grid, without identifying patterns related by symmetry).

(a) Determine a formula or effective procedure for computing C(m,n,N) for all positive integers m, n, N.
(b) For each fixed pair (m,n), determine the largest integer N = N_max(m,n) for which C(m,n,N) > 0.
(c) For each fixed integer N > 2, determine the smallest values of m and n (in an appropriate sense, e.g. minimizing m+n or the area mn) for which C(m,n,N) > 0.
artifact.status_search_result: No closed-form enumeration of C(m,n,N) appears in the literature. Available work on Golomb rectangles (Robinson, 1985 and later) provides bounds, special constructions, and computer searches for optimal cases, but the general counting problem and the determination of extremal m, n, N remain unresolved. The problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Golomb rectangles (Robinson, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 1985)
status_evidence.snippet: Examines two-dimensional arrays with constrained autocorrelation, with bounds and computational procedures but no general enumeration formula.
status_evidence.claim: The literature on Golomb rectangles addresses bounds and special cases rather than a general enumeration C(m,n,N).

status_evidence.title: Golomb Rectangles (ResearchGate)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Golomb's classes of radar/sonar arrays, with improved bounds and optimal cases.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work has improved bounds and identified optimal Golomb rectangles in particular cases, but does not give a general count.
